## 1) Run AUB autopilot (module-level) and select best
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
**What to check after:**
- Which candidates were generated and evaluated.
- Whether any candidate beats the current champion on the criteria you care about (usually lockbox is the “hard gate” and tuning is the “easy/progress” signal—depends on your system).
- Confirm “select-best” actually updated the champion pointer/file (or wrote a new champion artifact).

If this produces only regressions or noisy wins, it’s often a sign the module search space is exhausted or needs new candidate generators/constraints.

## 2) Run system autopilot (system-level candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
**What to check after:**
- Whether any system-level candidate improves **lockbox_mean** without tanking tuning (or vice versa, depending on your acceptance policy).
- Any failures due to integration issues (config mismatch, missing modules, incompatible versions). System-level runs often surface those.

If a system candidate looks strong, you’d typically promote it to champion via whatever promotion mechanism your framework uses (sometimes this tool does it; sometimes there’s a separate “promote” step).

## 3) Generate “next fix” guidance
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
**What to check after:**
- The prioritized list of failing/weak areas (often based on consistent error signatures or worst-case modules).
- Whether the suggested fix aligns with actual logs from the most recent runs (sanity-check it before acting).
